policy_title: Reduce Mental Health Waiting Times and Modernise Legislation
stated: Labour will bring down mental health waiting times and intervene earlier, recruiting an additional 8,500 new staff to treat children and adults in their first term, specifically trained to support those at risk of suicide. The new Young Futures hubs will provide open-access mental health services for children and young people. Labour will also modernise mental health legislation to give patients greater choice, autonomy, enhanced rights, and support, addressing discrimination against Black people, and ensuring dignity in treatment.

source.quote: Labour will bring waiting times down and intervene earlier. We will recruit an additional 8,500 new staff to treat children and adults through our first term. As part of our mission to reduce the lives lost to suicide, these new staff will be specially trained to support people at risk. Labour’s new Young Futures hubs will provide open access mental health services for children and young people in every community. Mental health legislation is also woefully out of date. The treatment of people with autism and learning difficulties is a disgrace. The operation of the Mental Health Act discriminates against Black people who are much more likely to be detained than others. Labour will modernise legislation to give patients greater choice, autonomy, enhanced rights and support, and ensure everyone is treated with dignity and respect throughout treatment.

bearing_set.reason: Policy directly targets mental health waiting times, recruits 8,500 staff, and creates open-access service hubs — all core healthcare-access indicators (waiting lists, mental health access, capacity).

Modernising mental health legislation to expand patient autonomy, enhance legal rights, address racial discrimination against Black people, and ensure dignity in treatment is a direct legal-rights framework change within O9's strict scope (equal treatment, due process, legal-rights framework).

Modernising mental health legislation to grant patients 'greater choice, autonomy, enhanced rights' directly reforms compulsory-detention and treatment-consent powers under the Mental Health Act — bodily autonomy and freedom from state coercion are core O10 indicators.

membership_note: Three clear bearings: healthcare capacity/access (O3), anti-discrimination and patient rights in law (O9), and patient autonomy/bodily freedom under reformed mental health detention law (O10). Fiscal cost of 8,500 new staff is real but policy text gives no funding/borrowing detail so O12 cannot be pinned to a concrete mechanism without speculation. Educational spillover from Young Futures hubs is incidental to O7, not primary.
